name: Lint

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: lint-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: .pre-commit-config.yaml

      - name: Install pre-commit
        run: python -m pip install pre-commit

      - name: Cache pre-commit environments
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pre-commit
          key: pre-commit|${{ env.pythonLocation }}|${{ hashFiles('.pre-commit-config.yaml') }}

      # no-commit-to-branch guards local commits; CI also runs on pushes to main.
      - name: Run pre-commit checks
        run: SKIP=no-commit-to-branch pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure

# SGLang-NVIDIA-Mega

## Introduction

**SGLang-NVIDIA-Mega** holds the NVIDIA megakernels of the [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) framework: for each model it covers, the code of its small-batch decode step and the kernels that only make sense inside such a step, which hand their outputs to each other through mailboxes and programmatic dependent launch instead of through per-op boundaries.

The package loads as an SGLang [general plugin](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/hardware-platforms/plugin.mdx) (the `sglang.srt.plugins` entry point) and is turned on with SGLang's `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` server flag. The package registers each model's spec with SGLang's megakernels framework (`sglang.srt.megakernels`). With the flag, SGLang checks the setup at argument resolution, before the weights load. After the model runner has prepared a covered model (before the KV cache is sized), SGLang builds the megakernel and replaces that model instance's `forward`, which runs each covered step itself and leaves every other step to the model's own forward. Every rank then logs `NVIDIA megakernel: active (…)`. Without the flag, SGLang runs untouched.

> **Experimental:** the kernels, the models and setups they cover, and the switch may change.

## Features

### Supported Models

| Model | GPU | Tensor parallel | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | GB300 (SM103) | 4 | DSpark target verify steps of 1 to 384 rows (batch 1 to 64 at 6 rows a request) |

Larger verify steps, prefill and extend run SGLang's standard path. The DSpark draft step runs on the plugin's draft spec.

### What a covered step runs

The step is the plugin's own code over the weights SGLang loaded (`deepseek_v41/runtime`): the embedding and the Engram hashes, then per layer the mHC boundary (`boundary/`), the attention (`attention/`), the MoE (`moe/`) and Engram (`engram/`), then the head and the logits (`logits/`). Each package has a stock implementation that reproduces SGLang's decode step bit for bit, and puts this package's kernels in where the slot plan (`plan.py`) gives them a width:

| Slot | Rows | Kernel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wo_b` + attention all-reduce + mHC post + next norm (`hop_a`, `hop_a_batch2`) | 1–16 | `wo_b` GEMM whose epilogue stores its rows into a Lamport mailbox on every rank, and a Lamport consumer that reduces them and runs the mHC post, combine and RMSNorm |
| Routed experts (`moe`) | 1–48 | A route kernel and a pair of block-scaled tcgen05 GEMMs with 8-row tiles; an expert chosen by more than 8 rows takes several tiles |
| Router top-k (`gate`, `gate_wide`) | 1–48 | One CTA per row, bit for bit SGLang's fused gate (including the vision-token routing) |
| Replicated embedding (`embed`) | 1–48 | SGLang's fused lookup on the whole table, all-gathered once at build; no all-reduce |
| Engram prefetch (`engram`) | 1–8 (batch 1) | Every Engram layer's lookup and WKV quarter on a side stream; their two all-reduces on the main stream (SGLang's TP group) |
| Attention and MoE all-reduce + mHC post + next norm (`two_shot`) | 49–384 | Two-shot exchange: each rank sends row t only to its owner rank (t mod 4), which sums the four partials in rank order and sends the row back; the MoE post also folds the top-k finalize and the shared-expert add, and quantizes the next input to MXFP8 where SGLang's fused post does |

With the megakernel on, the default 36 slots run: the ones above, the attention chain, `hop_b` (the MoE post on hop A's Lamport mailbox) with its triggers, and the DSpark draft step's 16 slots. `SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_SLOTS` (comma-separated) overrides that list for tests and bisecting; empty runs every step function's stock code. `draft_embed` runs only when listed there.

### Design

- **Built at load.** Buffers, kernels and tactics for every covered width are allocated and compiled when the model is loaded, before the KV cache is sized. Nothing is compiled or allocated inside a step.
- **Graph-safe coverage.** A step is covered by its forward mode and row count alone, so every rank decides the same and a captured graph replays the decision made at capture.
- **Fail-stop synchronization.** Every wait on another GPU has a deadline below SGLang's watchdog. A rank that misses it faults at address 0x0, so no token from a failed step is returned.
- **No silent fallback.** With `--enable-nvidia-megakernel`, an unsupported setup stops the server at startup, before the weights load, listing every reason; a model the loaded weights do not fit stops every rank after the load.

## Quick Start

### Requirements

- An SGLang with the megakernels framework (`sglang.srt.megakernels`, `--enable-nvidia-megakernel`)
- SGLang's CUDA 13 image: FlashInfer (its low-latency block-scaled GEMM as in 0.7.0 to 0.7.2), CuTe DSL (`nvidia-cutlass-dsl`) and the CUDA Python bindings
- 4 x GB300

### Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega.git
cd sgl-nvidia-mega
pip install -e .
```

### Usage

```bash
SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=rng,-dspark-accept-sample \
SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1 SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT=per_rank \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tp 4 \
  --ep-size 1 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --dsv4-attn-backend flashmla \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --enable-nvidia-megakernel
```

The three environment variables are required by the DeepSeek-V4.1 spec; without them the server stops at startup, naming each.

## Repository Structure

```text
sgl-nvidia-mega/
├── sgl_nvidia_mega/
│   ├── plugin.py          # registers the specs with SGLang's megakernels framework
│   ├── common/            # NVRTC builds and PDL launches; CuTe DSL sync primitives
│   └── deepseek_v41/
│       ├── spec.py          # the spec: the setups it serves and its build
│       ├── plan.py          # which kernel fills each slot, per width
│       ├── runtime/         # the build, the executor and its per-step state, the embedding
│       ├── boundary/        # the mHC between sublayers
│       ├── attention/       # the attention step
│       ├── moe/             # the MoE step
│       ├── engram/          # the Engram layers
│       ├── logits/          # the head and the logits
│       └── sm103/           # kernels and the build-time runner; no SGLang imports
├── benchmark/             # the static decode table behind the speed numbers
└── test/
    ├── unit/              # CPU: the plugin, the setup checks, the step loop and the SGLang contract
    ├── kernels/           # GPU: each kernel against SGLang's or FlashInfer's op, fail-stop
    └── e2e/               # GPU: serving accuracy, KL, passkey and fail-stop, switch on and off
```

## Testing

```bash
pytest test/unit               # CPU only
pytest test/kernels            # 4 x GB300
pytest test/e2e                # 4 x GB300, with SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_E2E_MODEL_PATH set
```

# Benchmarks

## Static decode table (switch on vs off)

`static_table.py` measures tokens per second per user at each batch size: ISL 8K, OSL 1K,
batch 1–64, one fresh server launch per arm. The two arms differ only by
`--enable-nvidia-megakernel` (every shipped slot; no `SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_SLOTS`).

Server (GB300, TP4, DSpark). Both arms run with the measured launch's environment:
the Engram prefetch needs SGLang's per-rank Engram host table (without the two host-table
variables the plugin is refused at startup with that reason). SGLang places the tables
only through its generic process NUMA membind (`SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2`), with no per-table
placement; the numbers were measured on nodes gated for free huge pages, with the page
cache evicted and the huge pages warmed before each launch. The TP sync setting was part
of every measured launch, and its share of the numbers was not measured separately.

```
SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=rng,-dspark-accept-sample \
SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1 SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT=per_rank \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 --ep-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --dsv4-attn-backend flashmla --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --max-running-requests 256 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
  [--enable-nvidia-megakernel]
```

The three `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` variables fix the acceptance length at 3.51, so both arms
run the same number of verify steps; never set them for an accuracy run. With DSpark
block 5 a verify step has 6 rows per request. The on arm runs the plugin's step at every
captured batch: batch 1–8 (6–48 rows) with the routed-expert GEMMs, and batch 10–64
(60–384 rows, 19 captured widths) with the two-shot attention and MoE posts (`plan.py`:
two-shot from 49 rows up to `MAX_ROWS`, 384). The off arm runs SGLang's standard path at
every batch.

Client, two passes per launch:

```
python benchmark/static_table.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --salt r1 --out on-1
python benchmark/static_table.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --salt r2 --reverse --out on-1
```

Report the mean of the two passes per batch.

Protocol:
- Both arms on one node.
- At least 2 fresh launches per arm, in palindrome order (on, off, off, on).
- Diff the two launch commands and environments before reading a number.
- Check the startup line `NVIDIA megakernel: active (DeepSeek-V4.1: …; widths [6, 12, …, 384]; …)` on every rank in the switch-on arm, and its absence in the switch-off arm.
- A difference inside the run-to-run band (≈ 1.5 % at batch 1 and 4, ≈ 1 % elsewhere) is not a result.

## Accuracy

`test/e2e/test_deepseek_v41_server.py` runs GSM8K-200 past the largest covered width, KL
of covered steps against the normal prefill path, and a passkey past the indexer's
candidate span. With `SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_E2E_URL` set it tests a running server, so the
same checks run against the switch-off arm; judge the switch-on numbers against that
arm's own band.

"""The plugin entry point on CPU: it registers each spec with SGLang's megakernels
registry and no hook on SGLang's code, except the parity test's own."""

import pytest
from sglang.srt.megakernels import spec as registry

from sgl_nvidia_mega import plugin


@pytest.fixture
def hooks(monkeypatch):
    from sglang.srt.plugins.hook_registry import HookRegistry

    monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "_REGISTRY", {})
    seen = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        HookRegistry, "register", lambda target, hook, kind: seen.append(target)
    )
    return seen


def test_register_registers_every_spec_and_no_hook(hooks, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv(plugin.PARITY_SORT_ENV, raising=False)
    plugin.register()
    assert registry._REGISTRY == dict(plugin.SPECS)
    assert hooks == []
    # the registered path resolves to the spec SGLang checks
    spec, why = registry.find_spec(architectures=[plugin.SPECS[0][0]], isa="sm_103")
    assert spec is not None, why


def test_the_entry_point_is_the_one_sglang_checks():
    import tomllib
    from pathlib import Path

    project = tomllib.loads((Path(__file__).parents[2] / "pyproject.toml").read_text())
    entry_points = project["project"]["entry-points"]["sglang.srt.plugins"]
    assert entry_points == {registry.ENTRY_POINT: "sgl_nvidia_mega.plugin:register"}

"""Fail-stop waits on 4 SM100-family GPUs (GB300): when one rank never joins, the ranks
that wait on it fault within their deadline instead of hanging: the Lamport consumer of
the wo_b publish (1-8 rows) and the two-shot hop (49-384 rows), whose deadline comes
from its build alone.

Each case runs its own torchrun, since a faulted rank leaves its CUDA context unusable.
Run with ``python test/kernels/test_deepseek_v41_fail_stop.py``.
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap
import time

import pytest
import torch

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- hops

FAULT_DEADLINE_S = 2.0
HOP_FAULT_WORKER = textwrap.dedent(
    """
    import os, sys, time
    import torch
    from sglang.srt.distributed import parallel_state as ps
    from sglang.test.test_utils import publish_build_topology

    case, deadline = sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2])
    rank, world = int(os.environ["RANK"]), int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
    torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
    ps.set_custom_all_reduce(True)
    ps.init_distributed_environment(world_size=world, rank=rank,
        local_rank=int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]), distributed_init_method="env://")
    publish_build_topology(tp_size=world, world_rank=rank)
    ps.initialize_model_parallel()
    tp = ps.get_tp_group()
    dev = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
    H, HC = 5120, 4
    if case == "lamport":
        from sgl_nvidia_mega.deepseek_v41.sm103 import all_reduce_mhc as m
        m.set_wait_deadline(deadline)
        hop = m.AllReduceMHC(hidden_size=H, hc_mult=HC, max_num_tokens=16, top_k=6, device=dev,
                             group=tp.device_group)
        rows = 6
        def run():
            x = torch.randn(rows, H, device=dev).bfloat16()
            return hop(x, torch.randn(rows, HC, H, device=dev).bfloat16(),
                       torch.rand(rows, HC, device=dev), torch.rand(rows, HC, HC, device=dev),
                       torch.rand(rows, HC, device=dev), torch.randn(H, device=dev).bfloat16(), 1e-6)
    elif case == "two_shot":
        # no set_wait_deadline: the hop's deadline is its build argument only
        from sgl_nvidia_mega.deepseek_v41.sm103.two_shot_mhc import TwoShotMHC
        hop = TwoShotMHC(hidden_size=H, hc_mult=HC, max_num_tokens=384, top_k=6, device=dev,
                         group=tp.device_group, deadline_s=deadline)
        rows = 64
        def run():
            x = torch.randn(rows, H, device=dev).bfloat16()
            return hop.attn_post(x, torch.randn(rows, HC, H, device=dev).bfloat16(),
                                 torch.rand(rows, HC, device=dev), torch.rand(rows, HC, HC, device=dev),
                                 torch.rand(rows, HC, device=dev), torch.randn(H, device=dev).bfloat16(),
                                 1e-6)
    run(); torch.cuda.synchronize()  # every rank joins once: compiled and healthy
    torch.distributed.barrier(group=tp.cpu_group)
    print(f"RANK{rank} HEALTHY", flush=True)
    if rank == world - 1:
        time.sleep(4 * deadline + 20)  # never joins the second hop
        os._exit(0)
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        run(); torch.cuda.synchronize()
        print(f"RANK{rank} NO-FAULT", flush=True)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"RANK{rank} FAULTED after {time.time() - t0:.1f} s: {type(e).__name__}", flush=True)
    os._exit(0)
    """
)


def _gpu4() -> bool:
    return (
        torch.cuda.is_available()
        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] == 10
        and torch.cuda.device_count() >= 4
    )


@pytest.mark.skipif(not _gpu4(), reason="needs 4 SM100-family GPUs")
@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", ["lamport", "two_shot"])
def test_a_missing_rank_faults_its_hop_peers_in_time(case, tmp_path):
    script = tmp_path / "worker.py"
    script.write_text(HOP_FAULT_WORKER)
    port = 29500 + (os.getpid() + 37 * len(case)) % 2000
    t0 = time.time()
    out = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "torch.distributed.run", "--nproc_per_node=4",
         f"--master_port={port}", str(script), case, str(FAULT_DEADLINE_S)],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600,
    )  # fmt: skip
    log = out.stdout + out.stderr
    assert log.count("HEALTHY") == 4, log[-4000:]
    # the waiting ranks fault (the kernel's store to 0x0 surfaces as a CUDA error);
    # none returns as if the hop had completed
    assert "NO-FAULT" not in log, log[-4000:]
    faulted = [l for l in log.splitlines() if "FAULTED after" in l]
    assert len(faulted) == 3, log[-4000:]
    for line in faulted:
        assert (
            float(line.split("after ")[1].split(" s")[0]) < 4 * FAULT_DEADLINE_S + 10
        ), line
    assert time.time() - t0 < 300


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider"]))

"""The switch on GB300 TP4 with DSpark: its stock step against SGLang's.

``TestStockStepIsSGLangs``: with every slot off, the covered step runs each package's
stock code, which must reproduce SGLang's decode step exactly.
``SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_PARITY`` (test only) runs SGLang's forward and then the
megakernel's on every eager verify step and logs the largest difference of the logits
and the hidden states; the sparse indices are sorted in both (their atomic emission
order is not deterministic). Batches of 1, 2, 4 and 8 requests cover 6, 12, 24 and 48
rows.
"""

import concurrent.futures
import os
import re
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import requests
from deepseek_v41_server import ARGS, ENV, MODEL, URL
from sglang.test.test_utils import (
    DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
    CustomTestCase,
    popen_launch_server,
    terminate_and_kill_process_tree,
)

from sgl_nvidia_mega.plugin import FLAG_CLI

LAUNCH_TIMEOUT = 3600
PARITY_ENV = {
    "SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_SLOTS": "",
    "SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_PARITY": "1",
    "SGLANG_NVIDIA_MEGAKERNEL_PARITY_SORT_TOPK": "1",
}
LINE = re.compile(
    r"NVIDIA megakernel parity \S+ rows=(\d+) logits_max_abs=(\S+) .*hidden_max_abs=(\S+)"
)
# a difference renders as "<max> (rel ...)"; equal tensors as "0 (rel ...)", absent as "n/a"
EQUAL = ("0", "n/a")


@unittest.skipIf(URL, "launches its own server with the parity switch")
class TestStockStepIsSGLangs(CustomTestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.logs = tuple(
            tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w+", suffix=s) for s in (".out", ".err")
        )
        cls.process = popen_launch_server(
            MODEL,
            DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
            timeout=LAUNCH_TIMEOUT,
            # eager verify steps: the parity check runs outside CUDA graphs only
            other_args=ARGS + [FLAG_CLI, "--disable-decode-cuda-graph"],
            env={**os.environ, **ENV, **PARITY_ENV},
            return_stdout_stderr=cls.logs,
        )

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        terminate_and_kill_process_tree(cls.process)
        for log in cls.logs:
            log.close()

    def _generate(self, i: int) -> str:
        r = requests.post(
            DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST + "/generate",
            json={
                "text": f"Question {i}: explain step by step whether {i} * 17 + 3 is odd.",
                "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 48},
            },
            timeout=600,
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["text"]

    def test_every_covered_width_is_bitwise(self):
        for batch in (1, 2, 4, 8):
            with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(batch) as pool:
                list(pool.map(self._generate, range(batch)))
        text = "".join(Path(f.name).read_text() for f in self.logs)
        found = LINE.findall(text)
        self.assertTrue(found, "no parity line: the covered steps did not run")
        diffs = [line for line in found if line[1] not in EQUAL or line[2] not in EQUAL]
        self.assertEqual(diffs, [], f"{len(diffs)} of {len(found)} steps differ")
        self.assertLessEqual({6, 12, 24, 48}, {int(rows) for rows, *_ in found})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

quant feeding wq_b on memory that holds garbage (``fill``: every ``torch.empty`` filled
with the poison byte; ``pool``: the allocator's blocks filled and freed first), the
output bit for bit the same as on zeroed memory, eager and replayed (``POISON`` lines).

The file name sorts first in test/kernels, so plain ``pytest test/kernels`` runs it
before any other kernel test allocates in the process: the ``pool`` cases need the
caching allocator to hand back the blocks they poisoned.

def _ll_gemm_ready() -> bool:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 10:
        return False
    try:
        import cutlass  # noqa: F401
        import flashinfer  # noqa: F401
    except ImportError:

needs_ll_gemm = pytest.mark.skipif(

# -------------------------------------------------------------- wq_b on poisoned memory

N, K = 8192, 1280  # wq_b at TP4: target and draft
POISON_EPS = 1e-6
# 1-8: plain swizzle; 9-48: row tiles (the target's 9-48, the draft's 10-45)
# a 128x4-scale width, the first row-tile width and the widest
ROWS = (6, 9, 48)
# 0xFF: NaN as an E4M3 code and as a UE8M0 scale; 0x7F: NaN code, scale 1.0
POISON = (0xFF, 0x7F)

_empty = torch.empty


@contextmanager
def _filled_empty(byte: int):
    """Every ``torch.empty`` in the block comes back filled with ``byte``."""

    def empty(*args, **kwargs):
        t = _empty(*args, **kwargs)
        t.view(-1).view(torch.uint8).fill_(byte)
        return t

    with mock.patch.object(torch, "empty", empty):
        yield


def _poison_pool(byte: int) -> None:
    """Fill and free small-pool blocks (up to 1 MB each) so the next allocations
    reuse garbage."""
    blocks = [_empty(1 << 19, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") for _ in range(64)]
    for b in blocks:
        b.fill_(byte)
    del blocks


def _poison_inputs(rows):
    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(rows)
    x = torch.randn(rows, K, device="cuda", generator=g).bfloat16()
    norm = (1 + 0.1 * torch.randn(K, device="cuda", generator=g)).bfloat16()
    w = torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", generator=g) / K**0.5
    w_q, w_sf = mxfp8_ll.quantize(w.bfloat16())
    return x, norm, w_q.contiguous(), w_sf.reshape(-1).contiguous()


def _step(x, norm, w_q, w_sf, mode, byte):
    """The chain's normalize_q_lora + compute_q_b on poisoned memory."""

    def run():
        _, q, s = rmsnorm_mxfp8(
            x, norm, POISON_EPS, pdl=True, row_tiles=x.shape[0] > mxfp8_ll.MAX_ROWS
        )
        return s, mxfp8_ll.linear(q, s, w_q, w_sf)

    if mode == "pool":
        _poison_pool(byte)
        return run()
    with _filled_empty(byte):
        return run()


@needs_ll_gemm
@pytest.mark.parametrize("graph", [False, True], ids=["eager", "graph"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["fill", "pool"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", ROWS)
def test_wq_b_output_ignores_unwritten_bytes(rows, mode, graph):
    x, norm, w_q, w_sf = _poison_inputs(rows)
    mxfp8_ll.precompile(w_q, [rows])
    # compile the norm outside any capture
    _step(x, norm, w_q, w_sf, "fill", 0)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    want_s, want = (t.clone() for t in _step(x, norm, w_q, w_sf, "fill", 0))
    for byte in POISON:
        if graph:
            g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
            with torch.cuda.graph(g):
                s, out = _step(x, norm, w_q, w_sf, mode, byte)
            g.replay()
        else:
            s, out = _step(x, norm, w_q, w_sf, mode, byte)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        unwritten = int((s != want_s).sum())
        nans = int(out.isnan().sum())
        same = torch.equal(out, want)
        print(
            f"POISON rows={rows} mode={mode} graph={graph} byte=0x{byte:02X} "
            f"scale_bytes={s.numel()} unwritten={unwritten} nan_out={nans} "
            f"bitwise={'yes' if same else 'NO'}"
        )
        assert same, f"wq_b output changed with poisoned memory 0x{byte:02X}"
        # a pass proves something only if the poison reached the bytes left unwritten
        if rows > mxfp8_ll.MAX_ROWS and byte == 0xFF:
            assert unwritten > 0, "poison did not land in the unwritten scale bytes"

        shared=(torch.zeros_like(shared) if shared_zero else shared).bfloat16(),
        x=torch.randn(rows, HIDDEN, generator=local).bfloat16(),

def _local_finalize(inp):
    rows = inp.gemm2.float()[inp.idx.clamp(min=0).long()]
    weights = torch.where(inp.idx >= 0, inp.weights, 0.0)
    routed = (rows * weights.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(1).bfloat16()
    return (routed.float() + inp.shared.float()).bfloat16()


def _torch_boundary(x, inp, group):
    y = x.float()
    dist.all_reduce(y, group=group)
    y = y.bfloat16().float()
    streams = inp.post.unsqueeze(-1) * y.unsqueeze(1) + (
        inp.comb.unsqueeze(-1) * inp.residual.float().unsqueeze(2)
    ).sum(dim=1)
    streams = streams.bfloat16()
    collapsed = (inp.pre.unsqueeze(-1) * streams.float()).sum(dim=1)
    normed = collapsed * torch.rsqrt(collapsed.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + EPS)
    return streams, (normed * inp.norm_weight.float()).bfloat16()

    torch.testing.assert_close(out[0].float(), streams.float(), atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2)
    if kind != "residual":

    if t.dtype == torch.bfloat16:
        bits = t.view(torch.int16).int()
        return torch.where(bits < 0, -(bits & 0x7FFF), bits)
    bits = t.view(torch.uint8).int()
    return torch.where(bits >= 0x80, -(bits & 0x7F), bits)

def _interleaved_plan(steps):
    plan = []
    for step in range(steps):
        rows = ROWS[step % len(ROWS)]
        kinds = ("a", "quant", "residual", "a_quant", "norm")
        plan += [(kind, rows, step % 2) for kind in kinds[: 3 + step % 3]]
    return plan


@torch.inference_mode()
@pytest.mark.parametrize("early", ["end"])
def test_hop_a_and_finalize_interleave_on_one_instance(env, early):
    hop = env.hops[early]
    inputs = {
        (rows, s): _inputs(rows, 300 + 10 * rows + s, env.rank, env.device)
        for rows in ROWS
        for s in (0, 1)
    }
    plan = _interleaved_plan(20)
    assert len(plan) >= 50 and len(plan) % 3

    def run(plan, late=None):
        outs = []
        for kind, rows, s in plan:
            if late == env.rank:
                torch.cuda._sleep(20_000)
            outs.append(_run(hop, kind, inputs[rows, s]))
        return outs

    # Reference: one hop at a time, every rank in step.
    reference = []
    for item in plan:
        reference += run([item])
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        dist.barrier(group=env.cpu_group)
    for (kind, rows, s), out in zip(plan, reference):
        _check_torch(kind, inputs[rows, s], out, env.group)

    def compare(outs, label):
        for index, (got, ref) in enumerate(zip(outs, reference[: len(outs)])):
            for a, b in zip(got, ref):
                assert _same(a, b), f"{label}: step {index} {plan[index]}"

    for late in (None, *range(env.tp)):
        outs = run(plan, late)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        compare(outs, f"back-to-back late={late}")

    # A graph of 22 hops (not a multiple of the 3 generations), replayed.
    sub = plan[:22]
    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.stream(stream), torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
        captured = run(sub)
    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
    for replay in range(20):
        graph.replay()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        compare(captured, f"graph replay {replay}")
        # Eager hops between replays move the generation the graph starts from.
        if replay % 4 == 3:
            compare(run(plan[:1]), "eager between replays")
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

        ],
        torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream,
    )
    return weights, ids


def _logits(kind, rows, gen):
    shape = (rows, TARGET_EXPERTS)
    if kind == "normal":
        return torch.randn(shape, device="cuda", generator=gen)
    if kind == "wide":  # both softplus branches (> 20 passes through)
        return torch.randn(shape, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 15
    if kind == "ties":  # few distinct values: ties broken by the lowest id
        return torch.randint(-3, 4, shape, device="cuda", generator=gen).float() * 0.5
    if kind == "correlated":  # the rows of one request choose overlapping experts
        base = torch.randn((1, TARGET_EXPERTS), device="cuda", generator=gen)
        return base + 0.2 * torch.randn(shape, device="cuda", generator=gen)
    if kind == "nan":
        x = torch.randn(shape, device="cuda", generator=gen)
        x[torch.rand(shape, device="cuda", generator=gen) < 0.01] = float("nan")
        return x
    raise ValueError(kind)


@needs_moe
@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["normal", "wide", "ties", "nan"])
def test_gate_topk_matches_moe_fused_gate(kind):
    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1234)
    for rows in [*range(1, 49), 64]:
        for trial in range(4):
            logits = _logits(kind, rows, gen).contiguous()
            bias = torch.randn(TARGET_EXPERTS, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 0.05
            valid = rows if trial % 2 == 0 else max(1, rows - 1 - trial)
            num_valid = torch.tensor([valid], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
            if trial == 2:  # no num_token_non_padded: every row is valid
                num_valid = None
            sw, sid = _stock(logits, bias, num_valid)
            fw, fid = _fast(logits, bias, num_valid)
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
            where = f"{kind} rows={rows} valid={valid} trial={trial}"
            assert torch.equal(fid, sid), where
            assert torch.equal(fw.view(torch.int32), sw.view(torch.int32)), where

def toolchain_reasons() -> list[str]:

    reasons = []
    for module, what in (

        ("flashinfer", "FlashInfer"),

    ):
        if importlib.util.find_spec(module) is None:
            reasons.append(f"needs {what}")
    digest = flashinfer_ll_gemm_digest()
    if digest is not None and digest not in FLASHINFER_LL_GEMM_SHA256:
        reasons.append(
            f"FlashInfer's {FLASHINFER_LL_GEMM} (sha256 {digest[:12]}) is not the "
            "low-latency GEMM the wo_b publish epilogue extends"
        )
    return reasons


def flashinfer_ll_gemm_digest():
    """The sha256 of the installed FlashInfer low-latency GEMM source, or None
    without FlashInfer (refused above)."""
    found = importlib.util.find_spec("flashinfer")
    if found is None or found.origin is None:
        return None
    path = Path(found.origin).parent / FLASHINFER_LL_GEMM
    if not path.is_file():
        return "missing"
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def _us(fn, iters=50) -> float:
    """Per-call time from CUDA graph replay, as the draft graph runs it (the CuTe DSL
    host launch path would dominate an eager loop)."""
    for _ in range(3):
        fn()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        for _ in range(iters):
            fn()
    graph.replay()
    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    start.record()
    for _ in range(5):
        graph.replay()
    end.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1e3 / (5 * iters)

    x = torch.randn(rows, K, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
    weight = head.lm_head.weight
    want = torch.matmul(x, weight.T).float()
    got = head(x)
    assert got.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and got.shape == (rows, N)
    got = got.float()

    assert rel <= sampler.LM_HEAD_LOGITS_REL, rel
    # greedy drafting reads the argmax; near-ties may flip, nothing else may

    top2 = want.topk(2, dim=-1).values
    near_tie = ((top2[:, 0] - top2[:, 1]) <= 2 * rel * want.abs().max()).sum().item()
    assert flips <= near_tie
    print(
        f"rows {rows}: rel {rel:.2e}, argmax flips {flips}; "
        f"low-M {_us(lambda: head(x)):.1f} us, "
        f"cuBLAS {_us(lambda: torch.matmul(x, weight.T)):.1f} us"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- sharded Markov chain

VOCAB = 129_280  # DeepSeek-V4.1
RANK = 256
STEPS = 5
MAX_BS = 8
KEY = 0x1234_5678_9ABC_DEF
TEMPERATURE_SETS = ((0.0,) * 8, (1.0,) * 8, (0.7, 1.3, 1.0, 0.0, 0.5, 2.0, 0.9, 1.1))
# Far above any launch, so only a missing peer reaches it.
DEADLINE_S = 20.0
ARRIVAL_WORDS = slice(128, 136)


def _markov_ready() -> bool:
    return (
        torch.cuda.is_available()
        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() in markov.SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES
    )


needs_gpu = pytest.mark.skipif(not _markov_ready(), reason="needs an SM100/SM103 GPU")


def _ternary(g: torch.Generator, device, *shape: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sparse {-1, 0, 1} BF16: |bias| <= 256, exact in BF16 in any summation order."""
    values = torch.randint(-1, 2, shape, generator=g)
    values *= torch.rand(shape, generator=g) < 0.25
    return values.to(device, torch.bfloat16)


def _reference(w1, w2, base, anchor, temperatures, offset, cache):
    """SGLang's MarkovSampleStep per step over the full vocab, as the unsharded draft runs it."""
    from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.dspark.markov_sample import MarkovSampleStep

    prev, tokens = anchor.long(), []
    for step in range(base.shape[1]):
        bias = F.linear(w1[prev], w2)
        prev = MarkovSampleStep.execute(
            base_logits=base[:, step],
            bias=bias,
            temperatures=temperatures,
            key=KEY,
            offset=offset,
            step=step,
            step_dtype=torch.float32,
            logits_out=None if cache is None else cache[: base.shape[0], step],
            has_sampled_rows=None if cache is not None else False,
        )
        tokens.append(prev)
    return torch.stack(tokens, 1)


def _assert_cache(cache, want_cache, temperatures, rows: int, what) -> None:
    """Rows that keep logits match; temperature-0 rows stay zero."""
    keeps = temperatures[:rows] != 0
    assert torch.equal(cache[:rows][keeps], want_cache[:rows][keeps]), what
    assert not cache[:rows][~keeps].any(), what


def _make(group, rank, world, w1, w2, max_bs=MAX_BS, keeps_logits=True):
    return markov.ShardedMarkov(
        embed_weight=w1,
        head_weight=w2,
        vocab_size=VOCAB,
        num_steps=STEPS,
        cache_dtype=torch.float32,
        group=group,
        rank=rank,
        world=world,
        max_bs=max_bs,
        deadline_s=DEADLINE_S,
        keeps_logits=keeps_logits,
    )


def _check_equal(device, group, rank: int, world: int, base_dtype, seed: int):
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    w1, w2 = _ternary(g, device, VOCAB, RANK), _ternary(g, device, VOCAB, RANK)
    chain = _make(group, rank, world, w1, w2)
    # A greedy draft's chain has no logit staging; it serves greedy blocks only.
    greedy_chain = _make(group, rank, world, w1, w2, keeps_logits=False)
    shard = slice(rank * VOCAB // world, (rank + 1) * VOCAB // world)
    offset = torch.tensor([3], dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    for rows in (1, 2, 4, 8):
        base = (torch.randn(rows, STEPS, VOCAB, generator=g) * 3).to(device, base_dtype)
        anchor = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (rows,), generator=g).to(device)
        for temps in TEMPERATURE_SETS:
            temperatures = torch.tensor(temps, device=device)
            for keep in (True, False):  # sampled draft vs greedy draft (no logits)
                want_cache = (
                    torch.zeros(MAX_BS, STEPS, VOCAB, device=device) if keep else None
                )
                want = _reference(
                    w1, w2, base, anchor, temperatures[:rows], offset, want_cache
                )
                for sampler in (chain,) if keep else (chain, greedy_chain):
                    for local in (True, False):
                        inputs = base[:, :, shard].contiguous() if local else base
                        for _ in range(3):
                            cache = (
                                torch.zeros(MAX_BS, STEPS, VOCAB, device=device)
                                if keep
                                else None
                            )
                            tokens = torch.full(
                                (MAX_BS, STEPS), -7, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
                            )
                            if keep:
                                sampler.launch_noise(rows=rows, key=KEY, offset=offset)
                            sampler.sample(
                                base_logits=inputs,
                                anchor_tokens=anchor,
                                temperatures=temperatures,
                                logits_cache=cache,
                                draft_tokens=tokens,
                            )
                            torch.cuda.synchronize()
                            what = (rows, temps, keep, local, sampler is chain)
                            assert torch.equal(tokens[:rows], want), what
                            if keep:
                                _assert_cache(
                                    cache, want_cache, temperatures, rows, what
                                )

    _check_forked_graph(device, chain, w1, w2, shard, base_dtype, g)
    assert int(chain.control[ARRIVAL_WORDS].abs().sum()) == 0  # arrivals reset


def _check_forked_graph(device, chain, w1, w2, shard, base_dtype, g):
    """CUDA graph: noise forked onto the side stream, replayed with new offsets."""
    rows = 2
    base = (torch.randn(rows, STEPS, VOCAB, generator=g) * 3).to(device, base_dtype)
    anchor = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (rows,), generator=g).to(device)
    temperatures = torch.tensor(TEMPERATURE_SETS[2], device=device)
    offset = torch.tensor([3], dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    cache = torch.zeros(MAX_BS, STEPS, VOCAB, device=device)
    tokens = torch.full((MAX_BS, STEPS), -7, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    local = base[:, :, shard].contiguous()

    def forked_sample():
        chain.fork_noise(rows=rows, key=KEY, offset=offset)
        chain.join_noise()
        chain.sample(
            base_logits=local,
            anchor_tokens=anchor,
            temperatures=temperatures,
            logits_cache=cache,
            draft_tokens=tokens,

def _synthetic_weight(n, k, gen):
    w = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", generator=gen) / math.sqrt(k)
    w_q, w_sf = mxfp8_ll.quantize(w.bfloat16())
    return w_q.contiguous(), w_sf.reshape(-1).contiguous()


def _activations(rows, k, gen, norm_weight=None):
    """Rows as a pre-norm feeds them to a projection: heavy-tailed channels (a few
    massive ones), RMS-normalized, times the norm weight; BF16."""
    gain = torch.exp(0.75 * torch.randn(k, device="cuda", generator=gen))
    gain[torch.randperm(k, device="cuda", generator=gen)[:8]] *= 30.0
    h = torch.randn(rows, k, device="cuda", generator=gen) * gain
    y = h * torch.rsqrt(h.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)
    if norm_weight is not None:
        y = y * norm_weight.float()
    return y.bfloat16()


def _cute_dsl(a, a_sf, w, w_sf):
    """SGLang's MXFP8 linear for block-FP8-as-MXFP8 weights (fp8_utils
    ``flashinfer_mxfp8_blockscaled_linear(backend="cute-dsl", pin_tactic=True)``)."""
    from flashinfer import mm_mxfp8
    from flashinfer.autotuner import autotune

    with autotune(False, skip_ops={"mxfp8_gemm"}):
        return mm_mxfp8(
            a,
            w.t(),
            a_sf.reshape(-1),
            w_sf,
            out_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
            use_8x4_sf_layout=False,
            backend="cute-dsl",
        )


def quantize_row_tiles(x):
    """FlashInfer's swizzled ``mxfp8_quantize`` of each 8-row tile on its own: codes
    [M, K] and the row-tile scale layout (one 128-row atom per tile, rows at its top)."""
    tiles = [mxfp8_ll.quantize(x[t : t + 8]) for t in range(0, x.shape[0], 8)]
    codes = torch.cat([q for q, _ in tiles])
    return codes, torch.cat([s.reshape(-1) for _, s in tiles])


def _ll(x, w, w_sf, tactic=None):
    """The plugin's arm: MXFP8 rows as the layer input arrives (plain swizzled scales
    up to 8 rows, row-tile scales past 8)."""
    if x.shape[0] <= mxfp8_ll.MAX_ROWS:
        a, a_sf = mxfp8_ll.quantize(x)
    else:
        a, a_sf = quantize_row_tiles(x)
    return mxfp8_ll.linear(a, a_sf.reshape(-1), w, w_sf, tactic=tactic), a


def _rel(out, ref):
    d = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs()
    return (d.norm() / ref.float().norm()).item(), d.max().item()

def _ckpt_tensor(root, index, name):

def _ue8m0_bytes(scale):
    if scale.dtype == torch.float32:
        return ((scale.view(torch.int32) >> 23) & 255).to(torch.uint8)
    return scale.view(torch.uint8)


def _kv_layers(source):
    """(label, wqkv_a weight, swizzled scales, attn_norm weight, kv_norm weight) per layer:
    wq_a and wkv stacked as SGLang fuses them, 32x32 UE8M0 blocks expanded to rows."""
    from flashinfer import block_scale_interleave

    if source == "synthetic":
        gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(17)
        w, w_sf = _synthetic_weight(*SHAPES["wqkv_a"], gen)
        attn_norm = torch.exp(0.3 * torch.randn(5120, device="cuda", generator=gen))
        kv_norm = torch.exp(0.3 * torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device="cuda", generator=gen))
        return [("synthetic", w, w_sf, attn_norm.bfloat16(), kv_norm.bfloat16())]
    root = os.environ.get(CKPT_ENV)
    if not root:
        pytest.skip(f"{CKPT_ENV} is not set")
    with open(os.path.join(root, "model.safetensors.index.json")) as f:
        index = json.load(f)["weight_map"]
    layers = []
    for layer in CKPT_LAYERS:
        p = f"layers.{layer}."
        get = lambda name: _ckpt_tensor(root, index, p + name)  # noqa: E731
        w = torch.cat(
            [get(f"attn.{m}.weight").view(torch.uint8) for m in ("wq_a", "wkv")]
        )
        scale = torch.cat(
            [_ue8m0_bytes(get("attn.wq_a.scale")), _ue8m0_bytes(get("attn.wkv.scale"))]
        )
        scale = scale.repeat_interleave(32, dim=0)
        assert w.shape == SHAPES["wqkv_a"] and scale.shape == (1792, 5120 // 32)
        w_sf = block_scale_interleave(scale.cuda().contiguous()).reshape(-1)
        layers.append(
            (
                f"layer{layer}",
                w.cuda().view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).contiguous(),
                w_sf.contiguous(),
                get("attn_norm.weight").cuda().bfloat16(),
                get("attn.kv_norm.weight").cuda().bfloat16(),
            )
        )
    return layers


def _freqs_cis():
    inv = 10000.0 ** (-torch.arange(0, ROPE_DIM, 2, device="cuda").float() / ROPE_DIM)
    angles = torch.arange(MAX_POS, device="cuda").float()[:, None] * inv[None, :]
    return torch.polar(torch.ones_like(angles), angles)


def _store(kv, kv_norm, freqs_cis, positions, loc, pages, layout):
    """SGLang's KV store kernel, as set_swa_key_buffer_radix_fused_norm_rope calls it."""
    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4 import fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla

    cache = torch.zeros(
        pages, layout.page_bytes(PAGE), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"
    )
    fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla(
        kv=kv,
        kv_weight=kv_norm,
        eps=EPS,
        freqs_cis=freqs_cis,
        positions=positions,
        out_loc=loc,
        kvcache=cache,
        page_size=PAGE,
        layout=layout.value,
    )
    return cache


def _regions(cache, loc, layout):
    """The tokens at ``loc`` by region: FP8 codes [T, n], the UE8M0 scale of each
    code's block [T, n], BF16 RoPE values [T, 64] or None, and the scale bytes."""
    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.kv_layout import KVLayout

    page, slot = (loc // PAGE).long(), (loc % PAGE).long()
    width, sb = layout.data_bytes, layout.scale_bytes
    data = cache[:, : PAGE * width].view(-1, PAGE, width)[page, slot]
    off = layout.scale_offset(PAGE)
    scales = cache[:, off : off + PAGE * sb].view(-1, PAGE, sb)[page, slot]
    # V4 (SGLang's default window cache): 448 FP8 nope in 64-value blocks, 64 BF16
    # RoPE values, 7 scales + a pad; V4.1: 512 FP8 in 32-value blocks, 16 scales
    if layout is KVLayout.V4:
        fp8, rope, block, nscales = data[:, :448], data[:, 448:576], 64, 7
        rope = rope.contiguous().view(torch.bfloat16)
    else:
        fp8, rope, block, nscales = data, None, 32, 16
    code_scale = scales[:, :nscales].repeat_interleave(block, dim=1)
    return fp8, code_scale, rope, scales[:, :nscales]


def _ordered(bits, sign_bit):
    """Sign-magnitude codes as integers whose difference counts representable steps."""
    bits = bits.long()
    mag = bits & (sign_bit - 1)
    return torch.where(bits & sign_bit != 0, -mag, mag)


@needs_ll_gemm
@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout_name", ["v4", "v41"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("source", ["synthetic", "checkpoint"])
def test_kv_bytes_tolerance(source, layout_name):
    """wqkv_a on the low-latency GEMM against SGLang's, through SGLang's KV store in
    each window-cache layout: FP8 codes in e4m3 steps (where both arms share the block
    scale), BF16 RoPE values in ulps, scale bytes exact or not."""
    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.kv_layout import KVLayout

    layout = KVLayout(layout_name)
    freqs_cis = _freqs_cis()
    pages = -(-max(KV_ROWS) * 4 // PAGE) + 1
    st = dict(tokens=0, cases=0, fp8=0, fp8_moved=0, rope=0, rope_moved=0)
    st.update(scales=0, scales_moved=0, kv_bf16_moved=0)
    max_steps, max_ulp, worst_rel = 0, 0, 0.0
    # peak-relative: a tiny change near zero spans many fine codes / ulps, so each region
    # is also measured against its coarsest quantum (FP8: the block's top-binade step,
    # 32 x the block scale; BF16 rope: the row's peak magnitude)
    max_top_steps, max_rope_rel = 0.0, 0.0
    for label, w, w_sf, attn_norm, kv_norm in _kv_layers(source):
        mxfp8_ll.precompile(w, list(KV_ROWS))
        for seed in range(SEEDS):
            gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(1000 + seed)
            for rows in KV_ROWS:
                x = _activations(rows, 5120, gen, attn_norm)
                a, a_sf = mxfp8_ll.quantize(x)
                ref = _cute_dsl(a, a_sf, w, w_sf)
                out, _ = _ll(x, w, w_sf)
                # each arm is bitwise across reruns (fixed tactics)
                assert torch.equal(_cute_dsl(a, a_sf, w, w_sf), ref), (label, rows)
                assert torch.equal(_ll(x, w, w_sf)[0], out), (label, seed, rows)
                worst_rel = max(worst_rel, _rel(out, ref)[0])
                positions = torch.randint(
                    0, MAX_POS, (rows,), device="cuda", generator=gen
                )
                loc = torch.randperm(pages * PAGE, device="cuda", generator=gen)[:rows]
                loc = loc.int()
                kv_ref, kv_ll = ref[:, Q_LORA:], out[:, Q_LORA:]
                args = (kv_norm, freqs_cis, positions, loc, pages, layout)
                c_ref, c_ll = _store(kv_ref, *args), _store(kv_ll, *args)
                assert torch.equal(_store(kv_ref, *args), c_ref)
                f_ref, cs_ref, r_ref, s_ref = _regions(c_ref, loc, layout)
                f_ll, cs_ll, r_ll, s_ll = _regions(c_ll, loc, layout)
                same_scale = cs_ref == cs_ll
                steps = (_ordered(f_ref, 0x80) - _ordered(f_ll, 0x80)).abs()
                st["fp8"] += f_ref.numel()
                st["fp8_moved"] += int((f_ref != f_ll).sum())
                shared = steps[same_scale]
                if shared.numel():
                    max_steps = max(max_steps, int(shared.max()))
                unit_ref = torch.exp2(cs_ref.float() - 127.0)
                unit_ll = torch.exp2(cs_ll.float() - 127.0)
                deq_ref = f_ref.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float() * unit_ref
                deq_ll = f_ll.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float() * unit_ll
                top_step = 32.0 * torch.maximum(unit_ref, unit_ll)
                max_top_steps = max(
                    max_top_steps, ((deq_ll - deq_ref).abs() / top_step).max().item()
                )
                if r_ref is not None:
                    ulp = (
                        _ordered(r_ref.view(torch.int16).long() & 0xFFFF, 0x8000)
                        - _ordered(r_ll.view(torch.int16).long() & 0xFFFF, 0x8000)
                    ).abs()
                    st["rope"] += r_ref.numel()
                    st["rope_moved"] += int((r_ref != r_ll).sum())
                    max_ulp = max(max_ulp, int(ulp.max()))
                    peak = r_ref.float().abs().amax(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-30)
                    rel = ((r_ll.float() - r_ref.float()).abs() / peak).max().item()
                    max_rope_rel = max(max_rope_rel, rel)
                st["scales"] += s_ref.numel()
                st["scales_moved"] += int((s_ref != s_ll).sum())
                st["kv_bf16_moved"] += int((kv_ref != kv_ll).sum())
                st["tokens"] += rows
                st["cases"] += 1
    print(
        "KV_TOLERANCE "
        + json.dumps(
            dict(
                layout=layout_name,
                weights=source if source == "synthetic" else list(CKPT_LAYERS),
                seeds=SEEDS,
                rows=KV_ROWS,
                cases=st["cases"],
                tokens=st["tokens"],
                kv_bf16_elements_moved=st["kv_bf16_moved"] / (st["tokens"] * HEAD_DIM),
                fp8_codes_moved=st["fp8_moved"] / st["fp8"],
                fp8_max_e4m3_steps=max_steps,
                fp8_max_diff_in_block_top_steps=max_top_steps,
                rope_bf16_values_moved=(st["rope_moved"] / st["rope"])
                if st["rope"]
                else None,
                rope_max_bf16_ulp=max_ulp if st["rope"] else None,
                rope_max_diff_over_row_peak=max_rope_rel if st["rope"] else None,
                scale_bytes_moved=st["scales_moved"] / st["scales"],
                wqkv_a_worst_norm_rel=worst_rel,
                reruns_bitwise=True,
            )
        )
    )
    # at most one step of the block's coarsest quantum (codes near zero move by more
    # fine steps for the same absolute change)
    assert max_top_steps <= 1.0, max_top_steps

def _make_cache(page, pages=11):
    """A padded V4 cache with poisoned unused bytes, and its dequantized values."""
    stride = page * 584 + 256
    raw = torch.full((pages, stride), 0x7F, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
    fp8 = torch.randn(pages, page, 448, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    exps = torch.randint(124, 130, (pages, page, 7), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
    rope = torch.randn(pages, page, 64, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
    tokens = raw[:, : page * 576].view(pages, page, 576)
    tokens[..., :448].copy_(fp8.view(torch.uint8))
    tokens[..., 448:].copy_(rope.view(torch.uint8))
    raw[:, page * 576 : page * 584].view(pages, page, 8)[..., :7].copy_(exps)
    nope = (
        fp8.float().view(pages, page, 7, 64) * torch.exp2(exps.float() - 127)[..., None]
    )
    values = torch.cat((nope.flatten(-2), rope.float()), -1).reshape(-1, 512)
    return raw.as_strided((pages, page, 1, 584), (stride, 584, 584, 1)), values

class _Core:
    """The step's attention metadata as the schedule reads it."""

    def __init__(self, rows: int, length_rows: int, seed: int):
        g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)

        def lengths(width):
            return torch.randint(
                1, width + 1, (length_rows,), generator=g, device="cuda"
            ).to(torch.int32)

        self.low_ratios, self.present_ratios = (1, 2), (1, 2, 4, 128)
        self.swa_page_indices = torch.zeros(
            rows, SWA_WIDTH, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
        )
        self.swa_topk_lengths = lengths(SWA_WIDTH)
        self._extra = {
            r: torch.zeros(rows, w, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
            for r, w in EXTRA_WIDTH.items()
        }
        self._extra_lengths = {r: lengths(w) for r, w in EXTRA_WIDTH.items()}
        self._fm = {r: backend._create_flashmla_metadata() for r in RATIOS}

    def get_flashmla_metadata(self, ratio):
        return self._fm[ratio]

    def sparse_page_indices(self, ratio):
        return self._extra[ratio]

    def sparse_topk_lengths(self, ratio):
        return self._extra_lengths[ratio]


def _lazy(core: _Core, rows: int) -> dict:
    """SGLang's per-layer build, with the layer's own query shape and matching."""
    q = torch.empty(rows, 1, 64, 512, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")

    def match(x, value):
        if x is None or x.shape[0] == rows:
            return x
        return (
            x[:rows]
            if x.shape[0] > rows
            else backend._pad_tensor_to_size(x, rows, value=value)
        )

    for r in RATIOS:
        extra = None if r == 0 else match(core.sparse_page_indices(r), -1)
        backend._maybe_precompute_flashmla_sched_meta(
            core.get_flashmla_metadata(r),
            q=q,
            indices=match(core.swa_page_indices, 0).unsqueeze(1),
            topk_length=match(core.swa_topk_lengths, 1),
            extra_indices=None if extra is None else extra.unsqueeze(1),
            extra_topk_length=None if r == 0 else match(core.sparse_topk_lengths(r), 1),
        )
    return {r: core.get_flashmla_metadata(r) for r in RATIOS}


def _view(core: _Core) -> SimpleNamespace:
    """The running forward's view (SGLang's ForwardView) over ``core``."""
    return SimpleNamespace(

def test_the_engram_prefetch_holds_the_reduced_rows_until_gather(monkeypatch):
    """reduce()'s all-reduced rows are read on the side stream after reduce() returns.
    An out-of-place all-reduce's record_stream does not keep them (the allocator ignores
    it on DLPack tensors), so the prefetch holds them until gather() joins wkv_done."""
    import gc
    import weakref

    waits, refs = [], []

    class Stream:
        def wait_event(self, event):
            waits.append((event, refs[-1]() is not None if refs else None))

        def wait_stream(self, other):
            pass

    class Event:
        def record(self, stream=None):
            pass

    class Rows:  # an out-of-place all-reduce result
        def record_stream(self, stream):
            pass  # what the caching allocator does for a tensor it did not allocate

        def __getitem__(self, j):
            return self

    def reduce_owned_rows(looked):
        out = Rows()
        refs.append(weakref.ref(out))
        return out

    main = Stream()
    monkeypatch.setattr(prefetch.torch.cuda, "current_stream", lambda: main)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        prefetch.torch.cuda, "stream", lambda s: contextlib.nullcontext()
    )
    engram = SimpleNamespace(
        embed=SimpleNamespace(_reduce_owned_rows=reduce_owned_rows)
    )
    layer = SimpleNamespace(
        engram=engram, n=4, cols=slice(0, 4), quarter=lambda rows: torch.ones(2, 4)
    )
    p = object.__new__(prefetch.EngramPrefetch)
    p.layers, p.stream, p.rows, p.hash_cols, p.dim = {3: layer}, Stream(), 2, 1, 4
    p.looked, p.parts = torch.zeros(8), torch.zeros(8)
    p.looked_up, p.reduced, p.wkv_done = Event(), Event(), Event()
    p.group, p.kv, p._emb = SimpleNamespace(all_reduce=lambda x: x), None, None

    p.reduce()
    gc.collect()
    assert refs[0]() is not None  # held past reduce(), while the side stream reads it
    p.gather()
    gc.collect()
    # still held when main waits for the side stream's WKV; released after
    assert (p.wkv_done, True) in waits and refs[0]() is None

"""SGLang's real init order for a DSpark server, as a CPU fixture.

``scheduler.init_model_worker`` builds a DSpark server in this order (STAGES):

- ``install``: the target model loads and the plugin builds (``install_megakernel``);
- ``draft_worker``: the DSpark worker's ``__init__``: ``attach_shared_modules`` gives
  the draft the target's embedding and head, then the decode phases resolve;
- ``memory_pools``: ``init_memory_pools`` -> ``alloc_memory_pool`` ->
  ``_init_post_memory_pool_components`` (KV pools, req_to_token, ngram / Engram
  history);
- ``attention_backends``: ``init_all_attention_backends`` (each runner's
  ``attn_backend``, target first, then draft);
- ``target_graphs``: the target runner's decode graphs (``decode_cuda_graph_runner``);
- ``draft_graphs``: the draft runner's graphs, with the draft sampler factory;
- ``overlap``: ``Scheduler.init_overlap``, after the model workers (the FutureMap).

``SchedulerInit`` hands out a worker whose objects gain those attributes only at their
stage. Reading one earlier raises ``EarlyRead``, which is not an ``AttributeError``:
``getattr(obj, name, default)`` and ``hasattr`` do not swallow it, so a slot that would
silently go inert on an early read fails too. A slot that reads worker or runner state
adds a ``Scenario`` to test_deepseek_v41_init_order.py.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import dataclasses
from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Callable, NamedTuple
from unittest import mock

import torch

STAGES = (
    "install",
    "draft_worker",
    "memory_pools",
    "attention_backends",
    "target_graphs",
    "draft_graphs",
    "overlap",
)
GAMMA = 5
CAPTURE_BS = (1, 2, 4, 8)
REQ_SLOTS = 16
HISTORY_WIDTH = 4
VOCAB, HIDDEN, TP = 128, 64, 4


class EarlyRead(AssertionError):
    """An attribute read before the init stage that sets it."""


class Staged:
    """An object whose ``later`` attributes appear at their stage; reading one before
    raises ``EarlyRead``, and unknown names raise ``AttributeError`` as usual."""

    def __init__(self, init: SchedulerInit, name: str, **now):
        object.__setattr__(self, "_init", init)
        object.__setattr__(self, "_name", name)
        object.__setattr__(self, "_later", {})
        for key, value in now.items():
            object.__setattr__(self, key, value)
        init.objects.append(self)

    def later(self, stage: str, **attrs) -> Staged:
        assert stage in STAGES, stage
        for key, value in attrs.items():
            self._later[key] = (stage, value)
        return self

    def __getattr__(self, name: str):
        # reached only when the normal lookup fails
        pending = object.__getattribute__(self, "_later")
        if name in pending:
            raise EarlyRead(
                f"{self._name}.{name} is set at stage {pending[name][0]!r}, read during "
                f"{self._init.stage!r}"
            )
        raise AttributeError(name)

    def _arrive(self, stage: str) -> None:
        for key, (at, value) in list(self._later.items()):
            if at == stage:
                object.__setattr__(self, key, value)
                del self._later[key]


def _attn_backend(pool):

    backend.__dict__.update(

        # SGLang's epilogue is built in the worker's __init__, before the phases
        epilogue = DsparkVerifyEpilogue(
            max_bs=max(capture_bs),
            verify_num_draft_tokens=width,
            device="cpu",
            tp_sync=self.tp_sync,
            fused_argmax=True,
            commit_ctx=CommitInjectCtx(
                draft_model=self.draft_model,
                block_pos_offsets=torch.arange(width),
                resolve_pool=lambda: self.draft_runner.token_to_kv_pool,
                # as SGLang's: the target runner's req_to_token (memory_pools)
                resolve_req_to_token=lambda: (
                    self.target_runner.req_to_token_pool.req_to_token
                ),
            ),
        )
        self.worker = Staged(
            self,
            "worker",
            gamma=gamma,
            verify_num_draft_tokens=width,
            _tp_sync=self.tp_sync,
            _verify_epilogue=epilogue,
            draft_model=self.draft_model,
            model_runner=self.target_runner,
            draft_model_runner=self.draft_runner,
        )

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def runtime_context(self):
        """SGLang's runtime context, published before any model loads: the parallel
        groups, the spec args and the graph config. Steps may patch over it."""
        group = SimpleNamespace(
            rank_in_group=0, world_size=TP, device_group=None, cpu_group=None
        )
        parallel = SimpleNamespace(tp_group=group, attn_cp_size=1, tp_size=TP)
        spec = SimpleNamespace(speculative_num_draft_tokens=self.gamma + 1)
        graph = SimpleNamespace(
            cuda_graph_config=SimpleNamespace(
                decode=SimpleNamespace(bs=list(self.capture_bs))
            )
        )
        with (
            mock.patch(
                "sglang.srt.runtime_context.get_parallel", return_value=parallel
            ),
            mock.patch("sglang.srt.runtime_context.get_spec", return_value=spec),
            mock.patch(
                "sglang.srt.runtime_context.get_exec",
                return_value=SimpleNamespace(graph=graph),
            ),
        ):
            yield

    def advance(self, stage: str) -> None:
        """Complete every stage up to and including ``stage``."""
        target = STAGES.index(stage)
        assert target >= STAGES.index(self.stage), (self.stage, stage)
        for at in STAGES[STAGES.index(self.stage) + 1 : target + 1]:
            for obj in self.objects:
                obj._arrive(at)
        self.stage = stage

    def run(self, scenario: Scenario) -> None:
        """Walk the stages in order and run each step after its stage completes."""
        self.slots = scenario.slots
        with self.runtime_context():
            for stage in STAGES:
                self.advance(stage)
                for at, step in scenario.steps:
                    if at == stage:
                        step(self)

def _linear(device, gen):
    from flashinfer import mxfp8_quantize

    w = torch.randn(HIDDEN, K, device=device, generator=gen) / math.sqrt(K)
    w_q, w_sf = mxfp8_quantize(w.bfloat16(), is_sf_swizzled_layout=True)
    return SimpleNamespace(
        weight=w_q.contiguous(),
        weight_scale_inv_swizzled=w_sf.reshape(-1).contiguous(),
        bias=None,
    )


def _activation(rows, device, gen):
    from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize

    x = torch.randn(rows, K, device=device, generator=gen).bfloat16()
    if rows > 1:
        # A zero row: zero outputs, whose negative zeros the publish clears.
        x[-1] = 0
    q, sf = flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize(x, is_sf_swizzled_layout=True, alignment=32)
    return q, sf.reshape(-1)


def _row_tile_activation(rows, device, gen):
    """Rows past 8 as the fused wo_a writes them for hop A: each 8-row tile quantized on
    its own, its scales the first 128-row atom of FlashInfer's 128x4 swizzle."""
    from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize

    from sgl_nvidia_mega.deepseek_v41.sm103.mxfp8_ll import RowTileMxfp8

    x = torch.randn(rows, K, device=device, generator=gen).bfloat16()
    x[-1] = 0
    codes, scales = [], []
    for start in range(0, rows, 8):
        q, sf = flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize(
            x[start : start + 8].contiguous(), is_sf_swizzled_layout=True, alignment=32
        )
        codes.append(q)
        scales.append(sf.reshape(-1)[: K // 128 * 512])
    return RowTileMxfp8(torch.cat(codes), torch.cat(scales))


def _flashinfer_gemm(linear, qa, tactic):
    """FlashInfer's own low-latency GEMM with ``tactic`` (output, valid tactics); past 8
    rows, which its runner refuses, the same kernel launched by mxfp8_ll."""
    from flashinfer.gemm import gemm_base

    from sgl_nvidia_mega.deepseek_v41.sm103 import mxfp8_ll

    a, a_scale = qa
    if a.shape[0] > mxfp8_ll.MAX_ROWS:
        out = mxfp8_ll.linear(
            a, a_scale, linear.weight, linear.weight_scale_inv_swizzled, tactic=tactic
        )
        return out, mxfp8_ll.offered_tactics(HIDDEN, K, mxfp8_ll.MAX_ROWS)
    out = torch.empty(a.shape[0], HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=a.device)
    major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(a.device)
    runner = gemm_base._cutedsl_low_latency_blockscaled_gemm_runner(
        major * 10 + minor, True
    )
    workspace = gemm_base._get_cache_buf(
        "mm_mxfp8_workspace", gemm_base.DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SIZE, a.device
    )
    inputs = [
        a,
        linear.weight.t(),
        a_scale,
        linear.weight_scale_inv_swizzled,
        torch.bfloat16,
        out,
        workspace,
    ]
    runner.forward(inputs, tactic=tactic)
    return out, runner.get_valid_tactics(inputs, None)


def _mixes(rows, device, rank):
    gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(7 + rank)
    return (
        torch.randn(rows, HC, HIDDEN, device=device, generator=gen).bfloat16(),
        torch.rand(rows, HC, device=device, generator=gen),
        torch.randn(rows, HC, HC, device=device, generator=gen) * 0.1,
        torch.rand(rows, HC, device=device, generator=gen),
        torch.randn(HIDDEN, device=device, generator=gen).bfloat16(),
    )


def _torch_boundary(x, mix, group):
    residual, post, comb, pre, norm_weight = mix
    y = x.float()
    dist.all_reduce(y, group=group)
    y = y.bfloat16().float()
    streams = post.unsqueeze(-1) * y.unsqueeze(1) + (
        comb.unsqueeze(-1) * residual.float().unsqueeze(2)
    ).sum(dim=1)
    streams = streams.bfloat16()
    collapsed = (pre.unsqueeze(-1) * streams.float()).sum(dim=1)
    normed = collapsed * torch.rsqrt(collapsed.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)
    return streams, (normed * norm_weight.float()).bfloat16()

def test_wo_b_publish_matches_separate_publish(rank):
    from sgl_nvidia_mega.deepseek_v41.sm103.all_reduce_mhc import AllReduceMHC
    from sgl_nvidia_mega.deepseek_v41.sm103.wo_b_publish import PublishingMxfp8Linear

    tp_size = ps.get_tp_group().world_size
    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{torch.cuda.current_device()}")
    with torch.inference_mode():
        arm = AllReduceMHC(
            hidden_size=HIDDEN,
            hc_mult=HC,
            max_num_tokens=16,
            top_k=6,
            device=device,
            group=ps.get_tp_group().device_group,
        )
        publisher = PublishingMxfp8Linear(arm)
        gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(1000 + rank)
        layers = [_linear(device, gen) for _ in range(2)]

        def boundary(x, mix):
            residual, post, comb, pre, norm_weight = mix
            return arm(x, residual, post, comb, pre, norm_weight, 1e-6)

        # Which path each boundary of a sequence takes (True: published). The
        # sequence crosses the three generations several times on both paths.
        pattern = (True, True, True, False, True, False, False, True, True)
        for rows in (1, 6, 8, 12, 16):
            make = _activation if rows <= 8 else _row_tile_activation
            qas = [make(rows, device, gen) for _ in layers]
            mix = _mixes(rows, device, rank)
            assert publisher.supports(layers[0], rows)
            assert publisher.prepare(layers[0], qas[0]) is not None
            if rows > 8:
                # a 128x4 pair past 8 rows stays on the linear's own path
                assert publisher.prepare(layers[0], tuple(qas[0])) is None
            _, valid = _flashinfer_gemm(layers[0], qas[0], None)
            by_split = {}
            for tactic in valid:
                by_split.setdefault(tactic[3], tuple(tactic))
            # The default tactic (what an untuned mm_mxfp8 runs) and the first
            # without split-K and with split-K 4 (both epilogue branches).
            tactics = list(
                dict.fromkeys(
                    [tuple(valid[0])] + [by_split[s] for s in (1, 4) if s in by_split]
                )
            )
            for tactic in tactics:
                expected_c = [
                    _flashinfer_gemm(layer, qa, tactic)[0]
                    for layer, qa in zip(layers, qas)
                ]
                for late in range(tp_size):
                    for index, published in enumerate(pattern):
                        li = index % len(layers)
                        if rank == late:
                            torch.cuda._sleep(20_000)
                        if published:
                            prepared = publisher.prepare(layers[li], qas[li])
                            x = publisher(layers[li], prepared, tactic=tactic)
                            assert torch.equal(
                                x.view(torch.int16), expected_c[li].view(torch.int16)
                            ), f"C differs: rows={rows} tactic={tactic}"
                            got = boundary(x, mix)
                        else:
                            got = boundary(expected_c[li].clone(), mix)
                        # The separate publish kernel on the same C, one boundary
                        # later, so the generations must line up across paths.
                        reference = boundary(expected_c[li].clone(), mix)
                        for a, b in zip(got, reference):
                            assert torch.equal(
                                a.view(torch.int16), b.view(torch.int16)
                            ), (
                                f"boundary differs: rows={rows} tactic={tactic} "
                                f"late={late} step={index}"
                            )
                torch.cuda.synchronize()

            # Against torch: the math SGLang's own fused attention boundary runs.
            c = _flashinfer_gemm(layers[0], qas[0], tactics[0])[0]
            streams, normed = boundary(
                publisher(
                    layers[0],
                    publisher.prepare(layers[0], qas[0]),
                    tactic=tactics[0],
                ),
                mix,
            )
            ref_streams, ref_normed = _torch_boundary(
                c, mix, ps.get_tp_group().device_group
            )
            torch.testing.assert_close(
                streams.float(), ref_streams.float(), atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2
            )
            torch.testing.assert_close(
                normed.float(), ref_normed.float(), atol=6e-2, rtol=3e-2
            )

            # One CUDA graph of published and separate boundaries, replayed.
            tactic = tactics[0]
            stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
            stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
            with torch.cuda.stream(stream), torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
                captured = []
                for index, published in enumerate(pattern):
                    li = index % len(layers)
                    if published:
                        prepared = publisher.prepare(layers[li], qas[li])
                        x = publisher(layers[li], prepared, tactic=tactic)
                    else:
                        x = _flashinfer_gemm(layers[li], qas[li], tactic)[0]
                    captured.append(boundary(x, mix))
            torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
            for _ in range(3):
                graph.replay()
                torch.cuda.synchronize()
                for index, outputs in enumerate(captured):
                    li = index % len(layers)
                    reference = boundary(
                        _flashinfer_gemm(layers[li], qas[li], tactic)[0], mix
                    )
                    for a, b in zip(outputs, reference):
                        assert torch.equal(a.view(torch.int16), b.view(torch.int16))
            torch.cuda.synchronize()

HIDDEN, HC, TOP_K, EPS = 5120, 4, 6, 1e-6
